list: Pearl Harbor National Memorial. 4.7. (13,971) Historic Sites. ...

text_blocks.snippet: Honolulu offers a blend of natural beauty and historical landmarks. Top spots include Diamond Head State Monument for panoramic views, the Pearl Harbor National Memorial to honor WWII history, and the bustling sands of Waikiki Beach.
snippet_highlighted_words: Diamond Head State Monument for panoramic views, the Pearl Harbor National Memorial to honor WWII history, and the bustling sands of Waikiki Beach

list.snippet: Pearl Harbor: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and step aboard the Battleship Missouri Memorial to experience WWII history firsthand.
'Iolani Palace: Tour the only official royal state residence in the U.S., located in Downtown Honolulu.
Bishop Museum: Explore the premier natural and cultural history institution in the Pacific, housing millions of Hawaiian artifacts.
Diamond Head (Lēʻahi): Hike a 0.8-mile trail to the summit of this iconic volcanic crater for sweeping views of the coastline.
Mānoa Falls: Take an easy 1.6-mile roundtrip hike through a lush bamboo rainforest to a 150-foot waterfall.
Tantalus Lookout: Drive up the forest reserve road for the best panoramic overlook of the city and coastline.
Waikiki Beach: The most famous stretch of sand in Honolulu, perfect for surfing, swimming, and lounging.
Ala Moana Beach Park: A sprawling, calm-water beach park with a large adjacent mall for local dining and shopping.
Kona Coffee Purveyors: Grab a morning pour-over and a famous pastry in Waikiki.
Duke's Waikiki: Enjoy live music and local classics on the beachfront for an iconic sunset vibe.
Helena's Hawaiian Food: Visit this James Beard-recognized spot for traditional Kālua pork and pipikaula short ribs.

text_blocks.snippet: For more details on planning your activities, visit the official Go Hawaii Travel Guide.
